newsitem.title: USA: NGC to record up to $28 mln Q1 charges.
newsitem.headline: NGC to record up to $28 mln Q1 charges.

text.p: NGC Corp said Thursday it plans to record charges of up to $28 million in the first quarter and, as a result, earnings will be substantially below analysts' forecasts of $0.28 a share.
NGC said the charges include hedging-related losses in its natural gas liquids business and a write-down on the cost of its natural gas liquids inventory.
It estimated the charge arising from hedging-related losses would be $8.0 million pre-tax, or $5.2 million ($0.03 a share) after tax.

It said the inventory charge will cut the weighted average cost of the inventory to reflect market prices as of March 31, 1997. Based on current liquids prices, the charge is estimated at between $10 million and $20 million pre-tax, it said. The after-tax estimate ranges from $6.5 million, or $0.04 a share, to $13 million, or $0.08 a share, it said.
NGC said the steep drop in natural gas liquids prices during the quarter significantly reduced operating margins in its natural gas liquids marketing business.
Its gas processing business also experienced lower operating margins due to the price drop, it said.

Chuck Watson, chairman and chief executive officer, said, "We will be unable to meet analysts' expectations for the first quarter of 1997, and reported earnings, including the charges, should be approximately $0.05 per share."
For the first quarter of 1996, NGC reported earnings per share of $0.26. Net income was $30.3 million, and operating revenues were $1.6 billion.

Watson said the company has taken steps to minimize similar exposure in the future and that, notwithstanding the lower expectations for the quarter, the outlook for the remainder of the year is positive.
NGC gathers, processes, transports and sells energy products and services in North America and the UK.
